newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish purchasing managers' index fell in July.
newsitem.headline: Swedish purchasing managers' index fell in July.

text.p: Swedbank and I&L said on Friday that their Swedish purchasing managers' index fell to 51.4 in July from 62.3 in June, breaking a six month upward trend.
"The lower level in July was probably due to the fact that July is a holiday month and many companies wind down their operations," a statement from Swedbank and I&L said.
"The index also fell in July last year. The picture for the purchasing managers' index over three months is showing a positive trend."
In July last year the index was 48.4.
A rising index indicates that the industrial economic cycle is improving.
The statement said that the only component of the index that was under the important 50 mark in July was production.
"This is due to a number of companies reducing production in July," it said.
"Orders continue to develop positively and are a good way over 50. It is export orders that are showing the strongest levels rather than orders from the home market."
